pr_title: Fix Curve3D baking up vectors for nontrivial curves.
pr_body:
The code was modified in 42aa539 to have a different basis vector, but this line was missed and caused up vectors to invert sometimes.

Fixes #81879

One-character bugfix by @kleonc, bisection and test case by me.

pr_comments: Is there a better macro to test for vectors being nearly equal? CHECK_EQ is nice because it shows the precise values that are incorrect, but it's inappropriate for precise floating checks.
The bug is also present in 4.1, should be safe for cherry-picking? :thinking:

issue_context.title: Path3D Up Vector miscalculation
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.2.dev4.mono.official [549fcce5f]

### System information

Godot v4.2.dev4.mono - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3619) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900KF CPU @ 3.70GHz (20 Threads)

### Issue description

Since somewhere around 4.1, when a point on a Path3D is moved on the Y-axis, it flips itself and all points after it upside-down:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/37983284/bb05a5f2-467e-49c8-8d82-fce8cdb420d7)

Moving one of the points that come before it on the X-axis seems to fix the problem?
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/37983284/57f167b3-efd7-4877-bea4-b1aae6ae9c00)

Though even this seems to have a few errors here and there: (from the repro project)
![record](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/37983284/f6bc42ae-8033-44bf-bb98-279390ef3c99)

Expected no flipping, as it worked in previous versions such as v4.0.3.stable.mono.official [5222a99f5] here:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/37983284/608e7bb4-7425-4263-b8ee-088f4db9d4ff)


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Path3D
2. Add 2 points at the same Y position
3. Move one of them on the Y-axis


### Minimal reproduction project

[PathBug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/12652576/PathBug.zip)
comments:
> The repro project let me bisect this to [42aa539](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/42aa5398d951dc709c892ef9f7afef6a0cf5d9ca), part of #72842.
> 
> The changes to curve.cpp look relevant.

Looking at these changes I think this line:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e3e2528ba7f6e85ac167d687dd6312b35f558591/scene/resources/curve.cpp#L1686
should have also been changed to accomodate the changed direction, specifically to something like:
```cpp
rotate.rotate_to_align(-frame_prev.get_column(2), forward);
```
as `-Z` basis vector should be now interpreted as forward.

(Haven't tested it at all, just looked at the changed code.)

> Looking at these changes I think this line:
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e3e2528ba7f6e85ac167d687dd6312b35f558591/scene/resources/curve.cpp#L1686
> 
> 
> should have also been changed to accomodate the changed direction, specifically to something like:
> ```c++
> rotate.rotate_to_align(-frame_prev.get_column(2), forward);
> ```

This fixes the repro case, I can try to figure out a regression test and make a PR?

review_comments:
Perhaps flipping the z-vector in baked_forward_vector_cache.set() at line 1579, rather than here, is a more correct place to fix that (although I haven't tested it yet).

There may be other places that need to be fixed besides 1579, but since the inversion occurred on the z-axis by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72842, the proper way to fix it is all the z-axes which are inverted, not the y-axis.
Flipping that z-vector does not appear to fix the bug.

AFAICT the forward vectors are calculated/stored correctly and #72842 haven't touched that. What it changed (or tried to change) was how such forward vectors are used for creating Basis "frames" (used for obtating up vectors). It was changed for calculating the initial frame but not for the following ones, specifically in here. So I do think that's the exact code which needed fixing

> Flipping that z-vector does not appear to fix the bug.

Perhaps there are more that should be inverted. Instead of all `next_point - prev_point` as forward, we should make `prev_point - next_point` as forward.

---

~Or passing `true` to the third argument of all `Basis::looking_at(forward, up, true)` in that would be one correct solution, although there is the weirdness of +Z being forward inside Curve3D.~

~It is almost equivalent to revert https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/72842/files#diff-59e6aa6d9ded671ff780f8aa82611c4a12b8e9533ec9d4da023c6dfaf54a7b4e for about Curve3D.~

This may not good because the direction of PathFollow will be flipped again.
Oh sorry, column(2) is z-axis, I mistakenly thought it is y-axis. This may not be a problem if so...?
